title: L1 extraction
summary: What the recommendation-extraction skill read out of ONE library entry, held beside it at `library/<entry>/l1-extraction/` when the same instance holds the entry, or at `l1-extractions/<entry>/` when the entry lives in another instance (smart-base's handbook extraction, whose source moved to who-iris on 2026-10-30, who-iris#107): the L1 A-Box graph (`l1.json`, JSON-LD against the WHO SMART L1 ontology), the L2 scenario candidates derived from it (`scenarios/scenario-candidates.l2.json`), and the curation, vocabulary and run context that produced them. A sub-graph of `library`: nested in an entry, it is published with the entry beside the entry's manifest; held apart, its own viewer (`scripts/gen-l1-extraction-pages.ts`) publishes it. It is never a folder named for an entry another library holds, which reads as a second copy of that entry and makes the library ingest refuse the duplicate slug.
validatorNotApplicable: It holds several node kinds typed in different places. Its two graph documents are JSON-LD that carry an `@context` and no `$schema`, so a per-family validator cannot select them; they are validated against the L1 ontology (and the `l1-library` extension) by `kg/src/validate.ts`, which `scripts/l1-recommendation-candidates.ts` runs on every write. Its other files are inputs and provenance of that run (`l1-recommendation-candidates/v1`, `l1-scenario-vocabulary/v1`, `folio-run-context/v1`, a curation YAML), each read and checked by the script that consumes it. One runnable validator here would grade all of them against whichever single shape it named.

avatar.reads: a page with a small graph drawn out of it — what was read out of a source, as linked nodes

rationale: Owner, 2026-10-12, bean 8pzh item 1 (where L1 extraction output lives): "a and b" — keep it committed beside the library entry AND publish it with the source — and: "why does b not happen already? if its a part of the KG it should be published." It did not happen because it was NOT part of the declared KG: `library/` is declared with the one typology `library`, whose nodes are an entry's manifest, sections and blocks, and `l1-extraction/` was plain files no typology named, so nothing published it. A kind of its own rather than families added to cat-harness's `library`: the L1 ontology and its recommendations are WHO SMART concepts, and cat-harness may not name them (the `web-annex` argument, one kind over). `within: "library"` because the output is always held INSIDE an entry and belongs to it; the library publisher (`cat-harness-tools/scripts/gen-library-viz.ts`) publishes every directory declared inside an entry whose kind is `within` library, so the declaration is what publishes it. `derived`: every file is written by `scripts/l1-recommendation-candidates.ts` or `scripts/l1-recommendation-scenarios.ts` from the entry and an agent-authored curation, and regenerated, never edited in place. Tone 199 is smart-base's own WHO blue.
